Documentation, auto-generated multi-language SDKs, and live JSON-RPC endpoints
MCP server for agents to discover and call published protocols
12 additional protocol onboardings over 12 months, 3 per quarter
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v
request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Tx3 by TxPipe, described as an open API layer for Cardano dApp protocols with developer and agent-facing infrastructure.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,308,000 ADA plus a 327,000 ADA contingency reserve over 12 months, with a total withdrawal of 1,684,050 ADA including a 49,050 ADA Intersect administration fee.
Tx3 is intended to provide a standard open-source interface to Cardano protocols through documentation, multi-language SDKs, and live RPC endpoints.
The proposal says there is currently no common interface mechanism across the Cardano ecosystem, forcing integrators to relearn each protocol and raising integration costs.
TxPipe has already put the developer layer into production with 5 protocols live on the Tx3 Protocol Registry through Catalyst Fund 14.
The proposal funds 12 additional protocol onboardings, at 3 per quarter, with full developer and agent coverage.

The proposal asserts that adding an MCP server, per-protocol tools, skills, and LLM-structured documentation will make Cardano protocols accessible to AI agents and strengthen Cardano's position for autonomous on-chain interaction.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The requested amount is stated not to breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
Audit, oversight, reporting obligations, and milestone-based disbursement controls are stated to be provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties.

TxPipe is stated to have received funding through 30 Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule, plus 2025 Intersect open-source maintenance funding being delivered on schedule.

summary: The document describes a 1,684,050 ADA treasury withdrawal administered by Intersect for TxPipe's Tx3 project, focused on standardized protocol interfaces, SDK/RPC generation, agent-facing documentation, an MCP server, and 12 protocol onboardings over 12 months.
